The scheduled wire vectors are copied byte-for-byte to the native repository's `internal/archive/testdata/teams-report-series/`. Assignment cases change one sibling field at a time while holding the persisted authority fixed; config hashing alone does not authenticate those fields. Calendar vectors cover daylight-saving gaps and folds, weekly cadence and monthly clamping. Timing vectors include overlapping periods, final-deadline clamping and the finite schedule limit. Rejections exercise query, schema, ACL and strict JSON boundaries.

The inventory is the complete list, including legitimate aliases, from Go 1.27.1's `lib/time/zoneinfo.zip`, generated from IANA tzdata 2026c (see Go's `lib/time/update.bash`, `CODE=2026c` and `DATA=2026c`). IANA states its time zone database is public domain; see https://data.iana.org/time-zones/tz-link.html. To update deliberately, use that exact Go release and run `unzip -Z1 "$(go env GOROOT)/lib/time/zoneinfo.zip" | LC_ALL=C sort`, review the name and alias diff, copy identical bytes to `internal/archive/iana_zone_names.txt` in the native repository, update both pinned hashes and run both vector suites. Scheduled publication also embeds the unmodified Go 1.27.1 `lib/time/zoneinfo.zip` (SHA-256 `b2d18a7c8fa8142097a48c99609fb3c92db5ee98bc740294e57eab8ae9f94779`) in each repository and loads TZif bytes directly, independently of the host. The installed archive was checked against the archive extracted from the official `go1.27.1.darwin-arm64.tar.gz` (SHA-256 `ee215d57e0ec269c60cc9ceca68e6bda321ba9ee5afe24f4b0988703c2d87d12`, verified against [Go downloads](https://go.dev/dl/)). Go's release script identifies both code and data as IANA 2026c. The archive's sorted names match the inventory exactly. Update both archives, inventories, hash assertions, and shared vectors together in a separately reviewed contract change; do not silently substitute host data. Legacy recurrence remains on its existing host timezone behavior. The version 4 contract remains permanently tied to 2026c; adopting different rules requires a new reviewed contract version. The service v4 runtime must use the pinned calendar for every boundary and acceptance assignment, including future issuance implementations. The separate 045 assignment-reader pinned selection and final-period clamp must land on both sides before activation. There is no ordinary v4 issuer or public admission in this standalone change; the hostile-Postgres runtime test seeds a synthetic v4 marker by temporarily disabling the requirements-binding trigger.

A start time in the second occurrence of a daylight-saving fold is rejected because this contract resolves repeated civil times to the earlier occurrence; period zero must equal the exact consented instant. An eventual scheduling preview must explain the ambiguity and ask for the first occurrence or another time. Later fold boundaries use the earlier occurrence and gaps advance to the first valid second.
